page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.medium is a general-purpose, ARM-based virtual machine instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features a single dedicated physical core utilizing the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The processor is equipped with 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory and a bundled 59 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume. Network connectivity is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the single-core architecture demonstrates notable strengths in specific single-threaded tasks. The instance achieves top-tier performance in single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 17.04 GB/sec and strong performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.23 GB/sec. Stress-ng single-core CPU performance and large-block read-only memory bandwidth both register in the average tier. However, the single-core limitation results in poor multi-core stress-ng and PassMark CPU scores. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks is also relatively low at 13.9 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m9gd.medium offers a balanced resource profile for entry-level workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation rather than shared-core burstable resources. The inclusion of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage provides a qualitative advantage for applications that require low-latency temporary storage without the overhead of network-attached volumes. This instance is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, single-threaded data processing tasks such as file compression and decompression, basic web serving, and development or testing environments that benefit from dedicated ARM64 execution.
description: Amazon Web Services m9gd.medium is a general-purpose, ARM-based instance featuring a single dedicated AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 physical core running at 3.3 GHz. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of memory, a 59 GB local NVMe SSD instance store, and a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. Operating under the Nitro hypervisor, the instance delivers strong single-threaded performance, highlighted by top-tier bzip3 decompression and strong gzip compression benchmarks. However, its single-core design limits multi-core and parallel processing capabilities, as reflected in lower multi-core stress-ng and PassMark CPU scores. The bundled local NVMe storage provides efficient, low-latency temporary storage, making this instance a cost-effective choice for dedicated single-threaded workloads, lightweight web serving, and basic data processing tasks.
